methodological_rigor.justification: TAPISTRY cohort D is a single-arm, open-label phase II study of atezolizumab in TMB-high (≥13 or ≥16 mut/Mb) advanced solid tumors with pre-specified primary endpoint (IRC-assessed ORR at ≥16 mut/Mb vs. a prespecified 10% threshold), registered protocol (NCT04589845), central independent radiologic review, and standardized RECIST v1.1 assessment. The Clopper-Pearson method for ORR confidence intervals and Kaplan-Meier for DOR, PFS, and OS are appropriate. The study evaluates multiple TMB cutoffs (≥13 and ≥16 mut/Mb) and assay types (FMI tissue, FMI blood, non-FMI local) in parallel, providing important assay harmonization data. Key limitations: single-arm design without a comparator precluding determination of relative efficacy; heterogeneous tumor type composition (29.1% colorectal cancer, a type known to respond poorly to PD-L1 blockade without MSI-H) may dilute the ORR; short median follow-up (9.8 months); MSI-H status not collected or analyzed; only one pediatric patient enrolled despite stated pediatric eligibility; and subgroup analyses (by tumor type, PD-L1 status, assay type) are exploratory and underpowered.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospective single-arm phase II study mapping to LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate: TMB-guided tumor-agnostic immunotherapy is established (pembrolizumab received FDA approval for TMB-high ≥10 mut/Mb tumors based on KEYNOTE-158), and the TAPISTRY study evaluates a higher TMB threshold for atezolizumab, providing data to potentially extend tumor-agnostic immunotherapy. The 22.3% ORR with not estimable DOR at ≥16 mut/Mb provides clinically meaningful data supporting atezolizumab use in this population. The finding of higher ORR with FMI tissue vs. blood assays highlights clinically important TMB measurement variability across assays. However, the lack of comparator arm, heterogeneous tumor types with known differential sensitivity, and short follow-up limit the strength of clinical conclusions.

reporting_quality.justification: The study follows CONSORT extension for single-arm trials: patient flow diagram (Fig. 1), eligibility criteria with complete details in supplementary methods, safety-evaluable and efficacy-evaluable population definitions, IRC-assessed and investigator-assessed endpoints, and CTCAE v5.0 safety reporting are all presented clearly. Primary endpoint with prespecified threshold (10%) is explicitly stated and tested. AEs in ≥5% and ≥20% are tabulated. Assay-specific ORR data are presented for all four assay types. PD-L1 subgroup data are reported with explicit small sample size caveats. Limitations including MSI-H data absence, TMB assay variability, and small subgroup sizes are transparently acknowledged. The study is registered and trial registration data are cited.

novelty_literature.justification: The concept of TMB-guided tumor-agnostic immunotherapy is well established (KEYNOTE-158, pembrolizumab approval), and the retrospective atezolizumab TMB analysis (Legrand et al. 2018) already showed similar findings. The main novel contributions of TAPISTRY cohort D are: (i) prospective validation of atezolizumab in a dedicated TMB-high single-arm trial with pre-specified endpoints, filling the gap between retrospective data and prospective confirmation; (ii) head-to-head comparison of FMI tissue vs. blood TMB assay performance in the same population, demonstrating clinically important differential response rates; and (iii) the PD-L1 TPS exploratory analysis suggesting additive predictive value of PD-L1 ≥1% beyond TMB in tumor types beyond NSCLC. These are meaningful but incremental contributions to the established TMB-immunotherapy literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with separate sections for study design, patient characteristics, primary endpoint analysis, efficacy by assay type, tumor type-specific efficacy, PD-L1 subgroup analysis, and safety. Tables provide granular data for each assay type and TMB cutoff. The discussion appropriately contextualizes the 22.3% ORR against prior atezolizumab TMB studies (MyPathway 38.1%; retrospective analysis 29.7%) and explains the potential contribution of the colorectal-heavy tumor composition. Limitations including MSI-H absence, TMB assay variability, and pediatric under-enrollment are explicitly and transparently acknowledged. The writing is precise and appropriate for a clinical oncology audience.

key_strengths: Prospective phase II single-arm study with pre-specified primary endpoint and central IRC-based response assessment providing Level 2b evidence for atezolizumab in TMB-high tumors across tumor types including pediatric patients

Clinically relevant assay comparison: ORR numerically higher with FMI tissue (33.9%) vs. FMI blood (14.1%) and non-FMI local (20.5%) assays, directly informing assay selection for TMB testing in clinical practice
Not estimable median DOR in responders suggests durable responses in the TMB-high subset who achieve response, consistent with the immunotherapy mechanism
Safety profile consistent with known atezolizumab toxicity, providing additional safety data in a tumor-agnostic, all-comer population with ≥1 prior line
key_concerns: Single-arm study without a comparator precludes determining whether atezolizumab is superior to standard-of-care in this biomarker-defined population; the 22.3% ORR can only be compared with historical estimates

Colorectal cancer (29.1% of cohort) is a tumor type known to respond poorly to PD-L1 monotherapy without MSI-H, yet MSI-H status was not collected or analyzed, making it impossible to determine whether responses in colorectal patients were MSI-H driven

Efficacy is modest (ORR 22.3%) with short median PFS (2.8 months) at both TMB cutoffs; many patients progress rapidly, suggesting that TMB alone is insufficient as a single predictive biomarker for atezolizumab
Short median follow-up (9.8 months) precludes mature OS and DOR analysis; only 15 months median OS at ≥16 mut/Mb compared with published pembrolizumab data from KEYNOTE-158
chief_reviewer.rationale: TAPISTRY cohort D provides prospective Phase II evidence for atezolizumab in TMB-high solid tumors with a 22.3% ORR meeting its prespecified threshold, and generates important clinical data on TMB assay variability and PD-L1 complementarity; Tier 3 placement is appropriate for a well-executed but single-arm confirmatory trial that provides incremental evidence in an established biomarker-therapy paradigm, with the assay comparison and tumor type-specific data being the most novel contributions.
